The stated global order requires stability and sufficiently small steps. Use exact subflows or subsolvers with sufficient order and compatible boundaries; symmetric subsolvers are needed for time symmetry. Boundaries: None for the two-component ODE. PDEs need compatible stage boundary data; inhomogeneous or time-dependent boundaries can reduce order. Units: h has time units; F and G have units of state/time. For linear systems hA and hB are dimensionless. The oscillator illustration is nondimensional. Small dedicated implementations and measured checks Advance a 32-point Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion problem to T=1 with matched inputs and subsolvers. Four step sizes check first-/second-order temporal convergence, reference sensitivity, reaction balance and failure on nonconvergence in a lightweight comparison. Scope and remaining work This measures temporal error of the adopted compositions at fixed space, including splitting and midpoint-reaction discretization errors. It is not an exact continuum solution, spatial convergence check or independent PDE-engine comparison. Reactions do not conserve u+v; positivity is observed only for the fixed input. Work is reported as actual subflow calls, without runtime rankings or universal Strang superiority. This additional comparison of the existing Schnakenberg problem changes neither physical-problem counts, the common 22 examples, old release criteria nor success history. Long-time patterns, 2D and general boundaries are outside scope. The preceding limitations describe earlier editions.
